input.strategy_title: Integrated GenAI model evaluation for RHOAI
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Customers adopting generative models on RHOAI have no supported way to answer
"is this model good enough for my use case?" inside the platform. Evaluation
today happens in ad-hoc notebooks with lm-evaluation-harness or vendor tools,
results live in spreadsheets, and nothing links an evaluation to the model
version that was actually deployed. We need a first-class evaluation capability:
run standard and custom benchmarks against models served on the platform,
persist results alongside the model version, and let users compare candidates
before promoting one to production.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | Users can launch an evaluation of a model served on the platform (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) against a selected benchmark suite. |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Standard benchmark suites (e.g. MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag exposed through lm-eval task names) are available out of the box. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | Evaluation results are persisted and linked to the Model Registry version of the evaluated model. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Users can define custom evaluation tasks (own datasets and metrics) and run them through the same flow. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | The Dashboard shows evaluation runs, their status, and per-benchmark scores, and allows side-by-side comparison of two model versions. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | Evaluations can be embedded as a step in a Data Science Pipeline so promotion flows can gate on scores. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Llama Stack's eval provider API is backed by the platform evaluation service, so agents/apps built on Llama Stack get the same results. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Evaluation runs record cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) for capacity planning. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Product documentation covers the evaluation workflow end to end, including custom task authoring. |

## Affected Components

- TrustyAI
- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry

## Out of Scope

- Human-preference (arena style) evaluation collection
- Automatic model promotion decisions — pipelines gate, humans promote
- Fine-tuning feedback loops driven by evaluation scores

## Open Questions

1. Execution engine: TrustyAI's LMEvalJob (Tech Preview) already wraps
   lm-evaluation-harness — do we build on it as the single execution path, or is
   a new evaluation service needed to also serve Llama Stack's eval provider
   API? Needs a technical investigation with a recommendation.
2. Result schema: what is the canonical result format persisted to Model
   Registry custom properties, and does it survive benchmark-suite version
   bumps? Prototype against real MMLU output before committing.
3. Benchmark dataset licensing: which standard suites can we redistribute in
   disconnected environments, and which must be fetched by the customer?

# Evaluation execution and result persistence on the LMEvalJob path

## Description

Conditional epic, planned under outcome A of the evaluation execution engine
investigation: TrustyAI's LMEvalJob (which already wraps lm-evaluation-harness) is
extended into the single execution path for platform evaluations. This epic
delivers the execution backend: launching evaluations of served models against
selected benchmark suites, running custom evaluation tasks through the same flow,
persisting results linked to the Model Registry version of the evaluated model, and
recording cost/duration metadata.

## Scope

- Extend the LMEvalJob-based execution so an evaluation can be launched against a
  model served on the platform (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) with
  a selected benchmark suite (standard out-of-the-box or user-defined custom task)
- Expose the launch/status/results interface that the Dashboard, the Data Science
  Pipelines evaluation step, and the Llama Stack eval provider build against
- Persist evaluation results to Model Registry custom properties on the evaluated
  model's version, in the canonical result schema, linking each run to the model
  version it evaluated
- Support user-defined custom evaluation tasks (own datasets and metrics) through
  the same launch flow as standard suites
- Record cost/duration metadata per run (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) for
  capacity planning

## Acceptance Criteria

- An evaluation of a model served via a KServe endpoint or a Llama Stack
  distribution can be launched against a selected suite and runs to completion
  with per-benchmark scores
- Results are persisted and linked to the Model Registry model version of the
  evaluated model, in the canonical result schema, and remain interpretable across
  benchmark-suite version bumps
- A user-defined custom evaluation task (own dataset and metrics) can be run
  through the same flow as a standard suite
- Each run records cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time)
- The launch/status/results interface is available for the Dashboard, pipeline
  step, and Llama Stack provider consumers
- Selected out-of-the-box suites are available to the execution path (bundled or
  customer-fetched per the licensing determination)

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (execution backend for launching evaluations of served models)
- HLR-3 (results persisted and linked to the Model Registry version)
- HLR-4 (custom evaluation tasks through the same flow)
- HLR-8 (cost/duration metadata recording)

# Evaluation execution and result persistence via a new evaluation service

## Description

Conditional epic, planned under outcome B of the evaluation execution engine
investigation: a new evaluation service is built as the platform's execution path,
serving both direct evaluation launches and the Llama Stack eval provider API.
This epic delivers the execution backend: the service, its launch/status/results
interface, running standard and custom benchmark suites against served models,
persisting results linked to the Model Registry version of the evaluated model,
and recording cost/duration metadata.

Because this branch builds a greenfield service with the full functional scope,
it risks exceeding the ~2-week epic size: if outcome B is selected, this branch
is decomposed further at resolution time (e.g. service core, persistence, and
provider backing as separate epics continuing the ID sequence) before
implementation is scheduled.

## Scope

- Build the evaluation service in the TrustyAI component's midstream repository
  (per the investigation's recommendation; if a new repository is recommended
  instead, this branch is extended with repo/license/Konflux onboarding work
  before this epic can start)
- Use lm-evaluation-harness as the benchmark execution engine, consistent with the
  platform's existing lm-eval task naming
- Launch evaluations against models served on the platform (KServe endpoints or
  Llama Stack distributions) with a selected benchmark suite (standard
  out-of-the-box or user-defined custom task)
- Expose the launch/status/results interface that the Dashboard, the Data Science
  Pipelines evaluation step, and the Llama Stack eval provider build against,
  including the service-side backing for the Llama Stack eval provider API
- Persist evaluation results to Model Registry custom properties on the evaluated
  model's version, in the canonical result schema, linking each run to the model
  version it evaluated
- Record cost/duration metadata per run (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) for
  capacity planning

## Acceptance Criteria

- An evaluation of a model served via a KServe endpoint or a Llama Stack
  distribution can be launched against a selected suite and runs to completion
  with per-benchmark scores
- The service backs the Llama Stack eval provider API surface with the same
  results as direct launches
- Results are persisted and linked to the Model Registry model version of the
  evaluated model, in the canonical result schema, and remain interpretable across
  benchmark-suite version bumps
- A user-defined custom evaluation task (own dataset and metrics) can be run
  through the same flow as a standard suite
- Each run records cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time)
- The launch/status/results interface is available for the Dashboard, pipeline
  step, and Llama Stack provider consumers
- Selected out-of-the-box suites are available to the execution path (bundled or
  customer-fetched per the licensing determination)
- If the service lands in a new repository, its build pipeline is green before
  this epic completes

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (execution backend for launching evaluations of served models)
- HLR-3 (results persisted and linked to the Model Registry version)
- HLR-4 (custom evaluation tasks through the same flow)
- HLR-7 (service-side backing for the Llama Stack eval provider API)
- HLR-8 (cost/duration metadata recording)

# Investigation: evaluation execution engine — extend LMEvalJob or build a new evaluation service

## Description

Resolves the strategy's first open question: whether the platform evaluation
capability builds on TrustyAI's LMEvalJob (Tech Preview, already wrapping
lm-evaluation-harness) as the single execution path, or whether a new evaluation
service is needed that can also serve Llama Stack's eval provider API. The
deliverable is a written recommendation, with an architecture sketch of the chosen
execution path and the consumer-facing interface (CR/API) that the Dashboard, the
Data Science Pipelines step, and the Llama Stack eval provider will build against.

## Scope

- Assess LMEvalJob's current capabilities and Tech Preview limitations against the
  full requirement set: standard and custom benchmark tasks, result persistence to
  Model Registry, cost/duration metadata recording, and backing the Llama Stack
  eval provider API
- Assess what a new evaluation service would require, including where it would live
  (the TrustyAI component's midstream repo vs a new repository — if a new
  repository is recommended, repo/license/Konflux onboarding epics must be added to
  that branch of the plan)
- Define the consumer-facing interface for launching evaluations and reading run
  status and results, sufficient for downstream consumers to build against
- Confirm the chosen path serves both direct evaluation launches and the Llama
  Stack eval provider API
- Record the decision as one of two bounded outcomes:
  - **Outcome A**: extend LMEvalJob as the single execution path
  - **Outcome B**: build a new evaluation service serving direct launches and the
    Llama Stack eval provider API

## Acceptance Criteria

- The recommendation document compares both options against the full requirement
  set with an explicit per-requirement verdict
- A single outcome (A or B) is selected and recorded with rationale
- The consumer-facing interface (CRD/API surface) is described at a level
  sufficient for the Dashboard, pipeline-step, and Llama Stack provider work to
  build against
- The recommendation identifies where the execution code lives (existing repo or
  new repo), and, if a new repo is required, the additional onboarding work is
  called out
- The recommendation is reviewed and accepted by the owning team

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (indirect — determines the execution path the launch capability builds on)
- HLR-7 (indirect — determines how the Llama Stack eval provider API is backed)

Addresses the strategy's open question 1 (execution engine).

# Investigation: canonical evaluation result schema for Model Registry persistence

## Description

Resolves the strategy's second open question: the canonical format for evaluation
results persisted to Model Registry custom properties on the evaluated model's
version. The schema is prototyped against real MMLU output before being committed,
and must survive benchmark-suite version bumps. Owned by the Model Registry team
because the persistence target (custom properties on ModelVersion entities) is
their extension point; the outcome is the data contract for the execution,
Dashboard, and Llama Stack provider work.

## Scope

- Run representative standard benchmark (MMLU) evaluations and capture the raw
  lm-evaluation-harness output
- Design the canonical result structure: per-benchmark scores, suite identity and
  version, run metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time), and the link to the
  evaluated model version
- Validate the structure against Model Registry custom properties (REST API,
  type/size constraints, queryability for comparison views)
- Confirm the structure remains interpretable when a benchmark suite is upgraded
  (versioned suite identity recorded with results)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A prototype persists real MMLU evaluation results to a Model Registry model
  version's custom properties and reads them back correctly
- The schema records suite name and version so persisted results remain
  interpretable after a benchmark-suite version bump
- The schema carries the cost/duration metadata fields (tokens, wall-clock, GPU
  time) required for capacity planning
- The schema recommendation is documented and agreed with the Model Registry team,
  and shared with the teams building the execution path, the pipelines evaluation
  step, Dashboard views, and Llama Stack provider

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (defines the persisted, version-linked result format)
- HLR-8 (defines the cost/duration metadata fields recorded per run)
- Enables HLR-5 (Dashboard reads the schema), HLR-6 (the pipelines evaluation
  step exposes scores in the schema), and HLR-7 (provider returns results
  in the schema)

Addresses the strategy's open question 2 (result schema).

# Investigation: benchmark dataset licensing for disconnected redistribution

## Description

Resolves the strategy's third open question: which standard benchmark suites can be
redistributed with the platform in disconnected environments, and which must be
fetched by the customer. The deliverable is a per-suite classification with cited
license terms and legal confirmation, which determines the scope of the
out-of-the-box benchmark suite catalog.

## Scope

- License review of the candidate standard suites (e.g. MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag and
  other lm-eval task families under consideration) and the datasets they load
- Classify each suite: redistributable in the product vs customer-fetched, with the
  governing license terms cited per suite
- Identify the fallback delivery mechanism for suites that cannot be redistributed
  (customer-supplied datasets in disconnected environments)
- Obtain legal confirmation of the redistribution determinations

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every candidate suite is classified as redistributable or customer-fetched, with
  the specific license terms cited
- Redistribution determinations are confirmed through legal review
- The final list of out-of-the-box (bundled) suites vs customer-fetched suites is
  produced and handed to the benchmark suite availability work as its input

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (determines which standard suites can ship out of the box)

Addresses the strategy's open question 3 (benchmark dataset licensing).

# Out-of-the-box standard benchmark suites

## Description

Delivers the standard benchmark suites out of the box so users can select them when
launching an evaluation, per the redistribution determinations from the benchmark
dataset licensing investigation. Suites are exposed through lm-eval task names,
consistent with the platform's existing lm-evaluation-harness integration.

## Scope

- Package the suites determined redistributable (e.g. MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag exposed
  through lm-eval task names) for delivery with the platform, including
  disconnected (no external network) environments
- Provide the delivery mechanism for suites that cannot be redistributed, so
  customers can supply those datasets themselves and run them through the same
  flow
- Surface the suite catalog (suite name and version) for selection in the
  evaluation launch flow and for display of per-benchmark scores
- Record suite identity/version consistently so persisted results remain
  interpretable across suite version bumps

## Acceptance Criteria

- An evaluation can be launched against each bundled standard suite in a
  disconnected environment without external network access
- A customer-fetched suite can be supplied by the user and selected through the
  same launch flow as bundled suites
- The suite catalog identifies each suite's name and version, and only suites
  cleared for redistribution are bundled
- Each bundled suite's packaged version matches the suite identity recorded in
  persisted evaluation results

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (primary — standard suites available out of the box)
- Supports HLR-1 (launch against a selected benchmark suite)

# Dashboard evaluation experience: launch, run status, scores, and version comparison

## Description

The Dashboard integration for the evaluation capability: users launch evaluations
of models served on the platform (KServe endpoints or Llama Stack distributions)
against a selected benchmark suite, view evaluation runs with status and
per-benchmark scores, and compare two model versions side by side. The Dashboard
reads run state via Kubernetes CRs and results via the canonical result schema
persisted on Model Registry model versions; it owns no data plane.

## Scope

- Evaluation section in the Dashboard: list of evaluation runs with status, and
  per-benchmark scores per run
- Launch flow: select a served model (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack
  distribution), select a benchmark suite (standard out-of-the-box or custom
  task), and launch the evaluation
- Side-by-side comparison view of results for two model versions
- Results rendered per the canonical evaluation result schema agreed for Model
  Registry persistence
- Consistent with existing per-component Dashboard integration patterns
  (navigation section, resource lists, creation forms, feature-flagged
  enablement via the dashboard config CR)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can launch an evaluation of a served model against a selected benchmark
  suite from the Dashboard and observe the run's status until completion
- Evaluation runs display their per-benchmark scores
- A user can select two model versions and view their evaluation results side by
  side
- Results render correctly per the canonical result schema, including runs
  recorded with cost/duration metadata
- Launch supports both standard suites and user-defined custom tasks

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (user-facing launch of an evaluation)
- HLR-5 (runs, status, per-benchmark scores, side-by-side comparison)

# Evaluation step in Data Science Pipelines

## Description

Enables evaluations to be embedded as a step in a Data Science Pipeline, so
promotion flows can gate on evaluation scores (humans make the promotion decision;
the pipeline gates on the score). The step launches an evaluation through the
platform's evaluation execution path and exposes the results as pipeline outputs.

## Scope

- A pipeline step/component that launches an evaluation of a served model against
  a selected benchmark suite through the platform evaluation capability
- Expose per-benchmark scores and pass/fail against configurable thresholds as
  step outputs, in the canonical result schema defined by the result-schema
  investigation, so downstream steps can gate on scores
- Consistent with the KFP v2 SDK component patterns already used by the platform
  (pipelines already orchestrate training, batch scoring, and evaluation-style
  flows)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pipeline run can include an evaluation step that executes against a served
  model and completes with per-benchmark scores available as step outputs
- A downstream step can gate on the evaluation step's scores (e.g. proceed only
  above a threshold)
- The evaluation step works with both standard out-of-the-box suites and
  user-defined custom tasks
- The step surfaces evaluation run status and failure reasons in the pipeline run
  view

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-6 (evaluations embedded as a pipeline step; promotion flows gate on scores)
